question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to install arbitrary manifest-defined stdio MCP commands and reuse matching global MCP declarations, or must both operations use a host-authorized broker/allowlist and explicit sharing grant?
rationale: This determines the permanent process-execution and cross-role ownership boundary; it cannot be safely inferred from implementation details or repaired mechanically without choosing the product security policy.

options.title: Define brokered and authorized ownership
options.body: Require a host-approved command broker or allowlist for stdio declarations and an explicit host grant before another Claw may reuse a global MCP server.

options.title: Accept manifest authority explicitly
options.body: Document that consent to a Claw package authorizes arbitrary stdio command registration and exact global declaration reuse, with the resulting trust model owned by maintainers.

options.title: Hold this experimental slice
options.body: Pause the MCP ownership feature until the RFC or a maintainer-approved policy specifies its execution and sharing boundary.

recommendation.title: Define brokered and authorized ownership
recommendation.body: Require a host-approved command broker or allowlist for stdio declarations and an explicit host grant before another Claw may reuse a global MCP server.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the assigned reviewer and has already reviewed the relevant source-config and lifecycle ownership contracts.
